status: Operations now has native queue/summary/queue-policy reads, an owner-local HTTP router and a fail-closed Next transport/SSR cutover for non-Field exceptions. Shared composition mounting, Records/People read-port implementations, the retained TypeScript policy/exception commands and the remaining legacy notification consumer keep the six Operations workflows partial.

scope.domain: packages/server-operations/src/domain/queue_read.rs owns the typed non-Field queue row, source view, policy row, event row, people option, workspace/detail projections and current summary. It reuses the existing Operations exception row and summarizer without changing the Field transition policy.
scope.application: packages/server-operations/src/application/queue_read.rs enforces records.read, the operations module, selected-context expiry, Company/branch/department scope arguments, a bounded visible-source filter, current People options and bounded history. It returns a scoped not-found for a hidden or foreign exception and fails closed on a mismatched or foreign source projection.
scope.adapters: packages/server-operations/src/adapters/queue_read.rs reads only Operations-owned relations (operations_exceptions, operations_exception_events and operations_queue_policies) inside a caller-owned serializable transaction. It excludes Field exceptions and Field-only policies, keeps the exact Company/branch/department predicate and bounds exceptions, policies and history. No cross-owner SQL is invented; Records source visibility and People labels are public application ports supplied by composition.
scope.http: packages/server-operations/src/adapters/operations_http.rs exposes GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/operations and GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/operations?id=. It validates exact registered Host/Holding targets, one bounded record id, rejects request bodies, returns private/no-store and no-referrer responses, and maps BusinessError to bounded statuses. Session resolution, selected Company scope, source visibility, People labels and the serializable unit stay behind OperationsHttpBackend.
scope.transport: packages/feature-operations/src/adapters/server/native-operations.ts validates ERPX_NATIVE_OPERATIONS_CONFIG (loopback only, no reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 or owned app ports, exact unique HTTPS Holding origins, unique Hosts/slugs/ids, 250..30000 ms), forwards the actual session cookie, Host, branch/department selectors and rendered-context CAS headers, and strictly validates every workspace/detail/event/source/policy/person/summary field plus the returned context identity and bounded response.
scope.ssr: packages/workplace/src/lib/native-operations.ts maps the retained WorkContext into the native page context. The Operations list and detail presenters require ERPX_NATIVE_OPERATIONS_CONFIG, read only through the native transport and return 503 NATIVE_OPERATIONS_UNAVAILABLE when it is absent, invalid or failing. There is no silent TypeScript owner-read fallback. The GET Operations route is also native and 503s without configuration. Field rendering remains on its existing native Field transport, but the Operations page/route still requires the Operations configuration before it can reach that path.
scope.notClaimed: No command cutover, shared composition mount, real Account/Records/People port implementation, browser journey, authenticated page render, staging or private production verification. No whole-workflow completion flag is changed.

a missing transaction is rejected and a read-committed transaction is rejected with OPERATIONS_SERIALIZABLE_REQUIRED
httpCases: actual ephemeral loopback Router serves workspace and detail, preserves Host/Holding/query forwarding and private/no-referrer/nosniff headers
unknown targets, duplicate ids, malformed percent encodings and empty ids fail before the backend; backend conflict maps to 409

detail preserves history and returns a scoped not-found for a hidden row
mismatched id, foreign Company or invalid source version fails closed with OPERATIONS_SOURCE_INVALID
serialized workspace keys match the Next transport contract

removedReadConsumers: The Operations list presenter no longer imports or calls operationsWorkspace from the TypeScript owner service; it reads the native workspace and 503s without native configuration.

The Operations detail presenter no longer imports operationsExceptionDetail or the nativeFieldException lookup for non-Field routing; it reads native Operations detail and only falls through to the existing native Field detail when the native Operations read returns a scoped 404 and the Field module is present.
The Operations API GET no longer calls operationsWorkspace or operationsExceptionDetail; it serves the native reader and 503s without configuration.
retainedWithConsumers: packages/server-operations/src/public/operations-exceptions.ts still exports operationsWorkspace and operationsExceptionDetail for retained TypeScript consumers, including server-collaboration staff notifications. Those consumers were not edited by this owner slice.

The POST Operations route and server-operations policy/exception writers remain TypeScript. Queue policy draft/review, exception open/acknowledge/start/resolve/approve/reject/close/reopen/assign/prioritize/escalate/cancel, idempotency, CAS, IAM/People/Records guards, audit/outbox and Field same-transaction behavior are unchanged.
The existing native Field operations read/commands and the field-service/operations endpoint remain the Field path. The new Operations router intentionally excludes Field rows.
The OperationsConsole keeps its retained POST client and command receipt handling; only the surrounding page/API reads moved to the native transport.

limits: No shared composition backend is mounted, so no production/private route serves the owner router. The HTTP test backend is a recording fake.

The Records source-visibility and People recipient ports are application contracts only; no production implementation exists in this slice. Composition must bind them before enabling ERPX_NATIVE_OPERATIONS_CONFIG.
Only non-Field sources are read. Field exceptions continue on the existing native Field transport.
No command cutover is included. The six Operations workflows remain partial because the TypeScript policy/exception writers and the collaboration notification read consumer remain.
No browser, authenticated SSR render, Next dev server, public URL, staging, private production or Cloudflare verification was run.
The root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, lockfiles, src/composition/**, docs/status/** and other owners' implementation were not edited. Cargo.lock is unchanged.
